title: Russia/Mongolia border → Mongolia (camel caravan) → China (Xinjiang) → Kazakhstan → Uzbekistan → Turkmenistan dead-end → backtrack to Bukhara → Kyzylkum / Karakalpakstan → Kazakhstan (Beyneu, Shetpe) → Caspian Sea swim → landfall Azerbaijan (Sea Breeze / Baku), 2017–2024

waypoints.name: Russia–Mongolia border crossing (crossing point not sourced)
waypoints.event: Enters Mongolia from Russia. Only the year (2017) and the fact he was in Ulaanbaatar on 8 Aug 2017 are sourced; the border post (e.g. Kyakhta–Altanbulag) is NOT sourced.

waypoints.name: Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia
waypoints.event: Arrives Ulaanbaatar; joins 'Steppes to the West' camel-caravan project (Baigalmaa Norjmaa). Camels trained at a camp west of the capital; caravan departs 'just before winter' 2017.

waypoints.name: Camel caravan dissolution point (location not sourced)
waypoints.event: Group fractures after ~1,000+ km (Karl: 'more than a thousand kilometres'; Explorersweb: 1,130 km). Angela Maxwell worked on the project 'From August to mid-December' 2017; by 25 Feb 2018 she wrote all members except Norjmaa had left. Exact place unknown.

waypoints.name: Mongolian desert, 'a couple of hundred kilometres from the Chinese border' (location not sourced)
waypoints.event: Karl walking alone with his cart ('The Beast') in Mongolian desert, battered by gales; father says he is a couple of hundred km from the Chinese border (date = report date).

waypoints.name: Mongolia–China border crossing (crossing point not sourced)
waypoints.event: Crosses into China alone, 2018.

waypoints.name: Xinjiang police stop / roadside tyre-repair shack (location not sourced; site only says security radiated 'out from Urumqi')
waypoints.event: Detained, gear searched, footage confiscated, told the walk was over; British Embassy intervened; allowed to continue on a mandated route with 24-h escort to the Kazakh border.

waypoints.name: China–Kazakhstan border crossing (crossing point not sourced)
waypoints.event: Enters (eastern) Kazakhstan. Year conflicts: 2018 (Explorersweb/Wikipedia) vs Karl's Aug 2024 remark '5 years after entering Eastern Kazakhstan' (implies ~2019).

waypoints.name: Almaty, Kazakhstan
waypoints.event: Meets partner 'Rika' in Almaty before pressing west. Departure from Almaty reported (onthegosolo) under July 2019 heading, but Uzbekistan entry reported as early June 2019 — see conflicts.

waypoints.name: Kazakhstan–Uzbekistan border crossing, 2019 (crossing point not sourced)
waypoints.event: Enters Uzbekistan ('early June 2019' per an unsourced Wikipedia edit quoted by onthegosolo).

waypoints.name: Samarkand, Uzbekistan
waypoints.event: Passes through Samarkand with Rika along the Silk Road.

waypoints.name: Bukhara, Uzbekistan (first passage, 2019)
waypoints.event: Passes Bukhara heading for Turkmenistan. Karl later calls Bukhara 'my last major waypoint in Uzbekistan before we entered Turkmenistan' — this becomes the 2023 continuity/restart point.

waypoints.name: Uzbekistan–Turkmenistan border (crossing point not sourced)
waypoints.event: Karl crosses alone (Rika could not, visa); 30-day Turkmen visa with government escort.

waypoints.name: Turkmenistan–Iran border (exact post not sourced) — furthest point of the abandoned Turkmen spur
waypoints.event: Reaches Iranian border as Turkmen visa expires; Iran visa refused. Dates conflict: father on 27 Aug 2019 'on the border'; El Informador '15 September'; Karl: 'By the end of 2019'.

waypoints.name: Ashgabat, Turkmenistan (flown out)
waypoints.event: Escorts hurry him to Ashgabat and put him on a plane; returns to Los Angeles, later Mexico. Equipment ('the Beast') left in an escort's garden in Turkmenistan.

waypoints.name: Bukhara, Uzbekistan (restart point, 2023)
waypoints.event: Walk resumes from Bukhara with Angela Maxwell ('Hitting the road 14/03/2023'). Backtrack abandons ~700 miles of Turkmen progress (Karl, 2021: 'losing almost 700 miles of progress').

waypoints.name: Nukus, Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan
waypoints.event: 'first major waypoint Nukus' after 543 km from Bukhara (date = WBH post date). Leaves Uzbekistan for visa renewal (visits Baku).

waypoints.name: Uzbekistan–Kazakhstan border (crossing point not named in source)
waypoints.event: Crosses into Kazakhstan after 441 km from Nukus (water cached along a 260 km stretch 'past the Arial Sea'). Date = WBH post date for the crossing; Beyneu reached on the 28th, 87 km later.

waypoints.name: Beyneu, Mangystau, Kazakhstan
waypoints.event: Arrive Beyneu; rest/resupply; back on road 7 Jul 2023.

waypoints.name: Shetpe, Mangystau, Kazakhstan
waypoints.event: Arrive Shetpe after 309 km from Beyneu (date = WBH post date). Visa bounce needed; swim later postponed to Aug 2024.

waypoints.name: Caspian swim start point, Kazakh coast ('near Aktau' per press; exact point not published)
waypoints.event: Walk from Shetpe reaches start point ~28 Apr 2024 (~300 km, 14–28 Apr 2024). Swim begins mid-August 2024: planned start 16 Aug; on 16 Aug Karl posted the team was leaving 'south to the start point'; 31-day duration ending 17 Sep implies start ~17–18 Aug. Coordinates = Aktau town centre as proxy ONLY; true start is probably elsewhere on the coast (Shetpe→Aktau by road is well under 300 km — unresolved).

waypoints.name: Landfall, Azerbaijan — Sea Breeze resort (Nardaran area, Absheron, Baku)
waypoints.event: 'Task Complete: 18:30 – 17/9/2024'. Team arrives on the coast of Azerbaijan; welcomed 'In the resort city of Sea Breeze' by Deputy Minister Mariana Vasileva (other outlets say 'in Baku'). Coordinates approximate (Sea Breeze resort area), exact landing point not published.

segments.notes: Russia border to Ulaanbaatar, 2017. Route not sourced.

companions: others of the Steppes to the West team
segments.notes: Camel caravan (10 Bactrian camels carrying gear; walking alongside — Karl's rules allow pack animals). Departed 'just before winter' 2017; Norjmaa: 'After the first month, we were in the Gobi desert in mid-winter.' Distance: >1,000 km (Karl site), 1,130 km (Explorersweb). Norjmaa (unverified secondary snippet) claims Karl left after about three days — conflicts with all Karl-side sources. Exact Gobi route unknown.
Solo with cart 'The Beast' through winter/spring 2017–18 across Mongolian desert. Route unknown.
China, 2018, into Xinjiang. Route (Inner Mongolia/Gansu or direct into Xinjiang) not sourced.

segments.route_detail: Police-mandated route with 24-hour escort, no camping (route itself not published)
segments.notes: Karl refused a vehicle ride to the border because it would break the rule; walked under escort to the Kazakh border.
Whether Rika walked the whole stretch is not explicit; Karl's site: 'Karl and Rika followed the Silk Road through Samarkand and ... Bukhara'.
Severe heatstroke and several days' hospitalisation somewhere in Uzbekistan in mid-summer 2019 (location not stated).
Walked in 2019 but later ABANDONED: the 2023 restart was at Bukhara, so everything west of Bukhara toward Turkmenistan became a dead-end spur.

segments.route_detail: Through the Karakum Desert with government escort (escort carried most gear)
segments.notes: Dead-end spur. Karl 2021: Plan B 'would involve backtracking to Uzbekistan losing almost 700 miles of progress'. Onthegosolo: 'all of the walking he did in Turkmenistan will have been for naught.'
'With my visa up I was hurried by my escorts to Ashgabat and put on a plane.' Transport mode to Ashgabat not stated (presumably vehicle).

segments.route_detail: Flight Ashgabat → Los Angeles (2019); waits in Mexico 2020–2023; flight Mexico → Tashkent; train Tashkent → Bukhara (2023)
segments.notes: Gear shipped from Turkmenistan/Tashkent to Bukhara; swim kit shipped to Aktau.

segments.route_detail: Through the Kyzylkum Desert (Explorersweb); 543 km per WBH. Road not named by source (A380 Bukhara–Nukus is the obvious candidate but UNSOURCED).
441 km; 260 km remote stretch with buried water caches, 'past the Arial Sea' to the Kazakh border. Road not named (likely across the Ustyurt via the A380 — UNSOURCED).
segments.notes: Resumed from Nukus ('Back to Nukus and back on the road', WBH post 1 Jun 2023). Temperatures to 45°C.

segments.route_detail: 'Roughly 300 km, in an approximate 10-day walk', 14–28 Apr 2024, Shetpe → swim start point (start point not named)
segments.notes: WBH post is dated '7/04/2024' yet describes 14–28 April — date format/typo ambiguity.

segments.route_detail: Kazakhstan → Azerbaijan across the Caspian; daily swim stages from support vessels; SPOT live tracker existed but track not recovered
segments.notes: ~16/18 Aug – 17 Sep 2024. Distance 288 km (most sources; Karl's own stats post per onthegosolo: 275.5 km). 31 days (Karl), 32 days at sea / 27 swimming days (Explorersweb), 41 days (Azerbaijani/Kazakh press). ~132 h 21 min swimming. Routine: ~3 h morning + 3 h afternoon (Explorersweb); planned ~10 km/day (5+5) (Tengrinews); Karl's site: 'six-to-nine-hour shifts'. Slept on boats. Support: Azeri Coast Guard + a 64-m ship (WBH Jun 2024) / 'a local support boat from the Kazakh port of Aktau and an Azerbaijani Coast Guard ship' (Karl site) / 'a warship and two regular vessels' (Tengrinews). Vessel names unknown. How each day's stopping position was recorded and resumed is NOT described in any source found.

waiting for swim logistics/permits; team moved back to Baku 1 Jun 2024 to work with Azerbaijani government; trained in Baku (Jul) and Aktau (Aug)

S1.title: Update (situation reports) — WestBound Horizons
S1.publisher: WestBound Horizons (Karl Bushby & Angela Maxwell; domain now hijacked — use Wayback snapshots 20240915085339, 20240923174331, 20250717205540, 20251001034217)
S1.quote: 27/03/2023 ... pack and ship the Beast and Athathen (Angela’s cart) to Bukhara, the starting point and my last major waypoint in Uzbekistan before we entered Turkmenistan. | 12/03/2023 Everything arrives in Bukhara ... Hitting the road 14/03/2023. | 8/04/2023 After a long and trying haul we reach the first major waypoint Nukus. ... 543kms | 1/06/2023 Back to Nukus and back on the road for the Kazakh border. ... We bury and cache water along a 260km stretch getting us past the Arial Sea and to the border with Kazakhstan. 441kms | 26/06/2023 We cross into Kazakhstan and cover the next 87kms arriving in Beyneu on the 28th. ... hitting the road on the 7/07/2023. | 18/07/2023 ... Arrive in Shetpe after 309kms. From here we need to renew the 30 day Kazakh visa so require another visa bounce. | 31 / 08 / 2023 ... we have had to delay the crossing until August next year. | 7/04/2024 April 14th -28th The team was joined by Erik Scheeres for the last push from Shetpe to the start point of the swim. Roughly 300 km, in an approximate 10-day walk. | 1/6/2024 ... The team will be supported by the Azeri Coast Guard and a 64-meter ship. The start date is now set for August 10th from the coast of Kazakhstan. | 17/9/2024 31 days, 288kms and over 132hrs of swimming, the team arrives on the coast of Azerbaijan to a warm welcome. | 09/04/21 ... By the end of 2019 I arrived on the border of Iran. With my visa up I was hurried by my escorts to Ashgabat and put on a plane. ... Plan B This would involve backtracking to Uzbekistan losing almost 700 miles of progress.

S2.title: Goliath Expedition Story & Route
S2.quote: Back across Russia and into Mongolia, Karl arrived in Ulaanbaatar on 8 August 2017. ... A training camp west of the capital spent five months preparing the animals ... Just before winter, the caravan set out and covered more than a thousand kilometres across the unforgiving steppe. ... The caravan dissolved. Karl left it behind and crossed into China alone. | In 2018, Karl crossed into China ... The police let him keep walking — under a strictly mandated route, a twenty-four-hour escort, no camping, and later no internet access — all the way to the Kazakh border. | Across the Kazakh border, Karl met up with Rika in Almaty before pressing west. ... Karl and Rika followed the Silk Road through Samarkand and the old trading hub of Bukhara, heading toward Turkmenistan. ... At the Turkmenistan border, visa restrictions forced a separation: Karl crossed alone. | Supported by two escort vessels — a local support boat from the Kazakh port of Aktau and an Azerbaijani Coast Guard ship ... They pushed forward in six-to-nine-hour shifts ... After thirty-one days at sea, 288 kilometres ... and more than 132 hours in the water, the team stepped ashore in Azerbaijan

S3.title: Hiking the World: Updates from the Road
S3.quote: But back in late 2017, a number of notable long-distance travelers elected to join forces in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. ... Joining Bushby, Norjmaa and the camels came two more long-distance masochists, Jamie Ramsay and Angela Maxwell. ... Bushby, Maxwell and Ramsay have all left the project, leaving Norjmaa to continue alone.

S4.title: Where in the World is Karl Bushby?
S4.quote: By the end of 2019, he had trekked through Turkmenistan to its border with Iran. ... But he couldn't get a visa into Iran, and his 30-day Turkmen visa had expired. ... Currently, Bushby is waiting out his COVID quarantine in Mexico.

S5.title: Karl Bushby and Angela Maxwell Swim Across the Caspian Sea
S5.quote: Over 32 days at sea, they spent 27 days swimming through dangerously rough seas and high winds.

S6.title: Karl Bushby Begins Home Stretch of 27-Year, Round-the-World Walk
S6.quote: In 2018, he crossed Kazakhstan and then made his way through Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. ... Bushby and Maxwell flew to Bukhara, Uzbekistan, and walked across the Kyzylkum Desert to the Caspian Sea. ... the 288km swim from Kazakhstan to Azerbaijan in October 2024.

S7.title: Karl Bushby Back in Europe, Begins Last Leg of Journey
S7.quote: From Russia, he crossed through Mongolia, China, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan — another hard one. ... He could not get a visa for Iran, and then COVID struck. ... swam 288km in stages to Azerbaijan
